**Notes from The Critic:**
- Nine weeks, **37 dish ratings; 32 of 37 at 4★+ (86%)**. Four "Cook again: No" verdicts plus the single 1★. **Weeks 07-27 and 08-03 added zero to either list — two consecutive clean weeks.**
- 🚨 **THE ONLY FAILURE OF WEEK 08-03 WAS A SUPPLY-CHAIN FAILURE, AND IT MUST NOT BE READ AS A FOOD FAILURE.** The Hungarian Beef Goulash arrived in the submission at **2★ / Cook again: yes** with this note: *"Sadly, I didn't get to experience this dish. The stew meat went bad before I could cook the dish… The meat was rancid after sitting in my fridge for 5 days. Had to redirect and go to panda express instead."* The 2★ scores a ruined weeknight. It is **deliberately absent from `Recipe_Ratings.md`**, absent from the low-rated list above, and absent from the Watch List. **The recipe is untested, carries no no-repeat penalty, and is eligible for immediate reuse** — and "Cook again: yes" says Sean still wants it. The actionable lesson is scheduling, not cooking: **do not place a highly perishable raw protein in the last slot of the week without a "freeze on arrival" instruction on the card.**
- **FORMAT BEATS PROTEIN — NOW SIX CONFIRMATIONS, AND THIS WEEK SUPPLIED THE CLEANEST ONE YET.** Pork chops scored 3★/No; **pork tenderloin medallions in mushroom gravy scored 5★/Yes with "wouldn't change anything."** Same animal, opposite verdicts. The prior five: ground pork fine while chops missed; Lomo Saltado missed while every other beef format hit; Greek meatballs missed on the tzatziki format while chicken was otherwise 5★; Cajun shrimp missed on a yogurt sauce; shrimp returned 4★ the moment the sauce changed. **Judge formats, sauces and techniques. For a two-serving skillet, a 10 oz vegetable load overwhelms the protein and sauce. **Recommendation to the Chef: treat ~6–8 oz as the ceiling for a single supporting vegetable in a 2-serving dish, and let the protein and sauce lead.**
- 🛒 **SOURCING IS NOW THE KITCHEN'S LARGEST SOURCE OF LOST STARS, AND IT HAS TWO DISTINCT FAILURE MODES.** Mode one, **cart-building gaps** (lemongrass, chorizo, honey, extra lemons) — mitigated by the move to the King Soopers app and by flagging identity ingredients. ## Harvested Facts — Sourcing, Equipment & Standing Requests

*Durable statements Sean made in his rating notes, rescued from the one channel that otherwise discards everything but stars. **This section is APPEND-and-supersede — the Critic never overwrites it wholesale** (unlike the auto-generated section above, which is replaced every Friday). Every entry cites the submission it came from, so it can be re-checked when it goes stale. Added by The Developer 2026-08-07; the Critic maintains it from its step 3.5.*

- **Grocery sourcing (2026-08-06, `Rate_Submission_2026-07-27`):** Sean has "officially moved away from Instacart as the source of truth" and now builds a **King Soopers pickup cart in the King Soopers app, working directly from the shopping list**. Too many discrepancies in the Instacart transfer; he is considering dropping Instacart entirely. → **@Chef:** write the shopping list for a human filling a cart by hand — exact counts, exact package sizes, clear product names a store search will match, and a flag on anything a substitution would break. Do not frame rules as Instacart workarounds. *(Note: the human-editable "Standing Preferences" section above still reads "King Soopers via Instacart" — left for Sean to update.)*
- **Standing request — Philly Cheesesteak (2026-08-06, `Rate_Submission_2026-07-27`):** Sean asked by name for the **cheesesteak filling served on a hoagie** at some point. → **@Chef:** apply the next time that dish is served, and note it in the menu intro.
- **Standing request — bell peppers (2026-08-06, `Rate_Submission_2026-07-27`):** **Season the peppers before the pre-cook.** Unseasoned peppers "kind of dulled the Philly cheese steak flavor." → **@Chef:** bake into the recipe card, not just the menu.
- **Technique that works — cornstarch crust (2026-08-06, `Rate_Submission_2026-07-27`):** Sean called it out unprompted — "that cornstarch gets such a nice crisp on the surface of the salmon." Dredging protein in cornstarch before the sear is proven; apply beyond salmon.
- **Technique that works — par-boiled broccoli (2026-07-06 submission):** Par-boiling before the sauté pan gave more tender broccoli and made the pan easier to clean after pulling the chicken. Sean's own mod on Garlic Butter Chicken Thighs & Broccoli (5★ twice).
- **Technique that works — baguette sauce-sopper (2026-07-20 submission):** Warmed baguette slices stood around the rim of the bowl to soak up sauce. Sean's own idea, called a "perfect use case." Reuse on saucy skillet and stew dishes.
- **Constraint of life — portions and reheat (2026-07-20 submission, restated since):** Two-portion meals, **one adult**, leftovers are next-day lunch — "almost my entire diet." → **@Chef and @Critic:** this is why reheat quality became a scoring dimension, and it is the single strongest signal in the record. Name the reheat method on every recipe card ("reheat 350°F oven 15 min" / "microwave, covered, 2 min").
- **Scoring behavior — Sean grades on a curve (2026-08-06, `Rate_Submission_2026-07-27`):** "a lot of fire dishes this week, so when comparing to the others, this one was less special." → **@Critic:** a 4★ in a strong week is not the same signal as a 4★ in a weak one; do not treat a single 4★ as a demotion.
- ⭐ **SLATE SIZE IS A BUDGET OF MEALS, NOT A COUNT OF DISHES (2026-08-09, stated directly to the Manager).** Sean's exact words on deleting the Korean braise from week 08-10: *"I got rid of the braised chicken dish entirely. I just feel like I was at one too many meals this week since I carried one over, and the roast is technically 4ish portions."* Three durable rules fall out of this, and they resolve a question the system has been getting wrong: **(1) a CARRIED-IN dish consumes a slot.** When a dish moves in from a prior week the slate does not become six — Sean will drop one to get back to five. The Chef and the Manager should expect a compensating drop, not treat it as an anomaly. **(2) High-yield dishes count for more than one meal.** The Mississippi Pot Roast is **~4 portions**, so it covers roughly two dinners plus lunches; a week built on one big-yield dish genuinely needs fewer other dishes. **(3) He will fix an over-full week by DELETING, not by pushing.** Every prior calendar edit on record was a move; this is the first outright deletion, and the trigger was slate size rather than dislike of the dish. → *@Chef: when a dish is carried in, or when the menu contains a 4+ portion roast/braise, build FOUR other dishes, not five. @Critic: a dish dropped for slate-size reasons is not a negative signal — never watch-list it.*
- **Weekend availability — fishing (2026-08-09, stated directly to the Manager):** Sean left Sat 08-15 deliberately empty because he is *"likely going on a fishing trip that day."* First occurrence on record. → *Do not backfill an empty Saturday, and do not read one as a scheduling failure. If Saturdays go empty repeatedly through the summer, treat it as a standing seasonal constraint and stop placing the weekend dish there.*

- 🚨 **SOURCING FAILURE — PERISHABLE PROTEIN HAS A FIVE-DAY CEILING (2026-08-11, `Rate_Submission_2026-08-03`).** Sean's words: *"The stew meat went bad before I could cook the dish. I think King Soopers dropped the ball on that one. The meat was rancid after sitting in my fridge for 5 days. Had to redirect and go to panda express instead."* This is the first time the kitchen lost an entire dinner to spoilage, and it cost the week a dish. The operative fact is the interval: **groceries arrive once, at the top of the week, and raw protein scheduled for Thursday–Sunday sits in the fridge for four to six days.** → **@Chef: never place a highly perishable raw protein (stew meat, ground meat, seafood, poultry) in the back half of the week unless the recipe card says "FREEZE ON ARRIVAL — thaw in the fridge the night before."** Roasts, cured items, and pantry-forward dishes belong in the late slots. → **@Critic: a dish lost to spoilage is a supply-chain data point, never a taste score.**
- **Store availability — King Soopers does not reliably stock ground lamb (2026-08-11, `Rate_Submission_2026-08-03`):** *"Probably would have been better with Lamb, but King Soopers didn't have any, so I substituted ground beef."* Single data point, but it is a statement about the store's shelves rather than a reaction to a meal, so it is worth carrying. → **@Chef: whenever a dish depends on a specialty protein or specialty ingredient, name a sanctioned fallback on the recipe card and the shopping list** ("ground lamb — if unavailable, 85/15 ground beef; the dish still works"). Sean will substitute anyway; telling him what to substitute is free. *(Related: this is the fourth consecutive week a defining ingredient went missing — lemongrass, chorizo, lamb, plus the earlier honey and lemons.)*
- 🥬 **Standing request — vegetable ratio (2026-08-11, `Rate_Submission_2026-08-03`):** *"Only thing I would suggest is fewer green beans. 10oz absolutely dominated the dish."* The first time a vegetable **quantity** rather than a vegetable **choice** cost a star. → **@Chef: for a 2-serving dish, treat ~6–8 oz as the ceiling for a single supporting vegetable. The protein and sauce lead; the vegetable supports.** Bake it into the recipe card, not just the menu note.
- **Reheat criterion confirmed working (2026-08-11, `Rate_Submission_2026-08-03`):** Sean volunteered *"reheated well"* as the second clause of his Thai Red Curry note, unprompted, on a card that named its reheat method. Second consecutive week a reheat outcome appears in the notes without being asked for. → **@Chef: keep naming the reheat method on every card — it is being read and followed.** → **@Critic: reheat remains a first-class scoring dimension.**

## Recipe Recycling Rules
*The Chef reads these when building the weekly menu.*

- ★★★★★ (5): Recycle every 3–4 weeks
- ★★★★ (4): Recycle every 5–6 weeks
- ★★★ (3): Recycle only if explicitly carried over
- ★★ (2) or below: Do not recycle unless Sean requests it
- "Cook again: No" overrides star rating — do not recycle regardless of score
